newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-IRISH STAR DANOLI REMAINS UNBEATEN OVER FENCES.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-IRISH STAR DANOLI REMAINS UNBEATEN OVER FENCES.

text.p: Ireland's latest equine hero Danoli remained unbeaten over fences when he landed a novice chase at Naas, County Kildare, on Saturday.
The gelding picked up a cut on a fetlock on his way to a workmanlike two-and-a-half length victory but trainer Tom Foley said: "He's all right."
A crowd of 4,500, more than double the normal, turned up to witness the performance of a horse many see as a possible future Cheltenham Gold Cup winner.
A brave and top class hurdler, Danoli is currently learning his trade over the larger obstacles.
Foley said: "He made one mistake five (fences) out. But he was careful and was looking at his fences which is what we wanted him to do. The most important thing was to keep him on his feet.

Jockey Tommy Treacy said that the 7-2 on-favourite had been "a bit too careful" over his fences. "But he's getting used to them," he added. "I was pleased enough with him even if he wasn't spectacular."
Danoli won his first race over fences eight days ago and will probably run next at Fairyhouse on December 1.
Danoli first caught the imagination of the racing public in 1994 when he landed the top novice hurdle race at Cheltenham and another big race at Aintree.
He thrilled the crowd again the following year when he won the Aintree race a second time despite fracturing fetlock bone in running.

Placed third and fourth in the last two Champion Hurdles at Cheltenham, Danoli was bought by Foley on behalf of owner Dan O'Neill for around $11,500. So far, the gelding has won 14 races and earned over $300,000 in prizemoney.
